name: Uyghur
variety: Standard Uyghur of Xinjiang (Central dialect: Ürümchi, Ghulja), Arabic script; Latin script (ULY) also in use
sources: Hahn, Reinhard F. (1991). Spoken Uyghur. University of Washington Press.
Hahn, Reinhard F. (1998). Uyghur. In Lars Johanson & Éva Á. Csató (eds.), The Turkic Languages. Routledge.
Engesæth, Tarjei; Yakup, Mahire & Dwyer, Arienne (2009). Teklimakandin Salam / Greetings from the Teklimakan: A Handbook of Modern Uyghur. University of Kansas.
Yakup, Mahire & Sereno, Joan A. (2016). Acoustic correlates of lexical stress in Uyghur. Journal of the International Phonetic Association 46(1), 61-77.
contrasts: eight vowels: /i/ without a back partner (older /i/ and /ɯ/ have merged), /y u/, /e/, /ø o/, /æ ɑ/
voiced versus voiceless aspirated stops and affricates
velar /k ɡ/ versus uvular /q ʁ χ/
stress can distinguish words (a stem plus an unstressable suffix against a plain stem)
vowel length is not written: long vowels come from loanwords and from the loss of coda /r/ and other consonants
allophony: /i/ is [i] in front surroundings and a centralised or back [ɨ ~ ɯ] next to uvulars and in back-vowel words; it is neutral in vowel harmony
high vowels are devoiced between voiceless consonants and word-initially before a voiceless consonant (ikki, pishiq, ishik)
/ɑ/ and /æ/ are raised to [e] or [i] in open syllables when they lose the stress to a suffix (bala, balilar; at, éti); the spelling shows this
voiceless stops are aspirated in onsets
voiced stops are devoiced in syllable-final position
/k/ and /q/ are fricatives [ç ~ x] and [χ] before consonants (mektep, aqsaq)
coda /r/ is weak and often dropped with lengthening of the vowel (tört [tøːt])
/w/ varies with [v]; /l/ is velarised next to back vowels
/f ʒ/ occur in loans; /ʔ/ begins words written with an initial vowel and marks syllable breaks
phonotactics: no onset clusters in native words
coda clusters are sonorant or fricative + obstruent (tört, xelq, dost)
backness harmony with neutral /i/ and /e/; rounding harmony in some high-vowel suffixes
loans and compounds often break harmony

stress.type: final by default, with morphological exceptions
stress.rule: Stress falls on the last syllable of the word; unstressable suffixes and particles (negative -ma/-me, question -mu, predicative endings) leave it on the syllable before them.
stress.cues: duration is the robust cue; intensity is less consistent; F0 does not mark word stress (Yakup & Sereno 2016)

rhythm.vowel_reduction: moderate: unstressed /ɑ æ/ in open syllables are raised to [e i], and high vowels are devoiced or dropped between voiceless consonants

length.notes: Long vowels are secondary and not written: they occur in Arabic and Persian loans and where coda /r/ or another consonant is lost. Geminates occur in numerals (ikki, yette, sekkiz, toqquz) and at morpheme boundaries. No published duration ratio is given here.

intonation.declarative: rise at the end of non-final phrases, fall at the end of the statement
intonation.yes_no_question: marked by the clause-final particle -mu; final pitch stays high or rises
intonation.wh_question: prominence on the question word, final fall
intonation.continuation: rise at the end of non-final phrases
intonation.accent_shape: stressed syllables are marked by length rather than by a pitch movement (Yakup & Sereno 2016)
intonation.notes: Sentence intonation is low confidence and follows the general pattern of the better described Turkic languages; Yakup & Sereno (2016) show that F0 belongs to the sentence level, not to the word.

phonation: devoiced high vowels between voiceless consonants

problems: no stress rule is set for ug, so the default penultimate stress applies (bala, kitab, uyghur are stressed on the first syllable); Uyghur stress is final by default
p t k are inherited from the Turkish table and are unaspirated; Uyghur voiceless stops are aspirated
i is always one short centralised vowel (length 100, F2 about 1660 Hz): no [i] versus [ɨ ~ ɯ] variants and no devoicing between voiceless consonants
no long vowels, and coda r is always a full trill
k and q stay stops before consonants, and voiced stops are not devoiced at the end of a syllable
unstressable suffixes and particles are not handled
good: Arabic-script and Latin (ULY) spelling are both accepted
the vowels æ, ø, y and the consonants q, χ, ʁ, ŋ, dʒ are present
vowel harmony and vowel raising follow from the spelling

notes: The glottal stop is mostly predictable (before word-initial vowels and between vowels in loans).
